definition_zh: 耐用的；持久的；耐久的
definition_en: able to last a long time without breaking or wearing out, or continuing for a long time without fading
core_image: 一双走过泥地与碎石、鞋底却仍未开裂的旧靴
scene: 那双旧靴子走过泥地和碎石，鞋底边缘只是磨白了一点。These boots are durable enough for daily work.
sceneCN: 这里 durable 是「耐用的」（第 1 个义项：经得起长期使用而不损坏）；句意是这双靴子足够耐用，适合日常干活。

pos.zh: 形容词：耐用的；持久的；耐久的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「耐久性；耐用性」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「耐久地；持久地」
与 durable 同出拉丁语 durare，义为「持续时间；时长」

senses.title: Able to last without breaking
senses.definition: made to last a long time and to resist wear, pressure or damage
senses.definitionCN: 经得起长时间使用，能抵抗磨损、压力或损坏
senses.example: These boots are durable enough for daily work.
senses.exampleCN: 这双靴子足够耐用，适合日常干活。
senses.why: Latin durare meant to last, so durable describes an object that keeps its shape under use.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 durare 意为「持续」，所以 durable 形容一件在反复使用中仍能保持原形的物品。

senses.title: Continuing for a long time
senses.definition: lasting a long time without fading, weakening or ending, as a peace or a relationship
senses.definitionCN: 长时间持续而不消退、不减弱、不终结，如和平或关系
senses.example: The two countries signed a durable peace agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 两国签署了一份持久的和平协议。
senses.why: The same 'lasting' quality is applied to agreements and feelings, where what must resist wear is time rather than friction.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「耐久」品质被用到协议与感情上，那里要抵抗磨损的不是摩擦，而是时间。

senses.title: Goods that last, in economics
senses.definition: used of goods, such as cars or washing machines, that are expected to be used for several years
senses.definitionCN: 用于汽车、洗衣机等预期可使用数年的商品
senses.example: Durable goods such as washing machines are taxed differently.
senses.exampleCN: 洗衣机等耐用品的征税方式有所不同。
senses.why: Economists needed a label for goods that survive many uses, and the adjective became a fixed category.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家需要给能经受多次使用的商品一个标签，这个形容词于是成了固定类别。

intro.en: Durable comes from Latin durare, to last, through Old French; the whole family also gives duration and endure.
intro.cn: durable 经由古法语来自拉丁语 durare（持续），同一词族还给出 duration 与 endure。

items.en: Latin durus meant hard, firm or tough, and it is the adjective behind the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 durus 意为「坚硬的、结实的」，是整个词族背后的形容词。

items.en: The verb durare meant to last, to endure or to remain hard, and it supplied the idea of continuing through time.
items.cn: 动词 durare 意为「持续、忍耐、保持坚硬」，提供了「贯穿时间而延续」的观念。

items.en: The adjective durabilis meant lasting or durable and passed into French as durable.
items.cn: 形容词 durabilis 意为「持久的、耐久的」，后来进入法语作 durable。

items.en: Old French durable carried the sense of lasting and resisting wear into English.
items.cn: 古法语 durable 把「持久、抗磨损」的含义带进了英语。

items.en: Middle English durable was used for materials and for promises that were meant to hold.
items.cn: 中古英语 durable 用于材料，也用于本当守住的承诺。

items.en: Economics fixed durable goods as a category, while ordinary speech kept durable for anything that survives hard use.
items.cn: 经济学把 durable goods 固定为类别，日常语言则用 durable 形容任何经得起折腾的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin lasting family; the near-meaning group separates lasting, sturdy and tough by what they resist.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「持续」词族的词；近义组按所抵抗的对象区分 lasting、sturdy 与 tough。

entries.definition: The quality of lasting or resisting wear; durable plus -ity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「耐久性、耐用性」，由 durable 加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: In a lasting or durable manner; durable plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「耐久地、持久地」，由 durable 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The length of time something continues; from Latin durare.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「持续时间、时长」，来自拉丁语 durare。

entries.definition: To suffer something or to last through it; from Latin indurare, related to durus.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「忍受、持续」，来自与 durus 相关的拉丁语 indurare。

entries.definition: Continuing for a long time; close to durable but with less emphasis on resistance to wear.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「持久的」，接近 durable，但较少强调抗磨损。

entries.definition: Strong and solidly built; it stresses resistance to force more than length of use.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「结实的」，更强调抗外力而非使用年限。

entries.definition: Not easily broken or damaged; broader and more informal than durable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「坚韧的」，比 durable 更宽泛、更口语。

entries.definition: Able to recover shape or strength after pressure; it stresses bounce-back, not just survival.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有弹性的、能恢复的」，强调受压迫后回弹，而不只是撑住。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect Latin durare, to last, with boots, peace treaties and durable goods.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把拉丁语 durare（持续）与靴子、和平协议和耐用品连在一起。

normal.en: Latin durare is to last, so durable means able to keep going.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 durare 是「持续」，所以 durable 就是「能一直撑下去」。

normal.en: Durability is the noun, durably the adverb: the family keeps the same idea.
normal.cn: durability 是名词，durably 是副词，这一族保留同一个观念。

normal.en: The same root gives duration, which is time lasting, and endure, which is lasting through hardship.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 duration（持续的时间）与 endure（熬过艰难而持续）。

normal.en: A durable boot survives mud; a durable peace survives years.
normal.cn: 耐用的靴子熬过泥泞，持久的和平熬过岁月。

normal.en: Durable goods are things a household expects to keep for years, not weeks.
normal.cn: 耐用品是家庭预期会用上几年而不是几周的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a boot sole that has crossed the same gravel for ten years and still holds its shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鞋底在同一片碎石上走了十年，仍然保持原形。

abstract.en: Draw the same line under a peace treaty: the paper is thin, but the agreement does not wear through.
abstract.cn: 把同一条线画在一份和平协议下：纸很薄，协议却没有被磨穿。

abstract.en: Durable is about time failing to break something, whether it is leather, metal or a promise.
abstract.cn: durable 讲的是时间没能弄坏某物，无论那是皮革、金属还是一个承诺。

examples.en: These boots are durable enough for daily work.
examples.cn: 这双靴子足够耐用，适合日常干活。

examples.en: The two countries signed a durable peace agreement.
examples.cn: 两国签署了一份持久的和平协议。

examples.en: Durable goods such as washing machines are taxed differently.
examples.cn: 洗衣机等耐用品的征税方式有所不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: dur- 是「坚硬、持续」：durable 是经得住用的，duration 是持续的时间，endure 是熬得住。

root: 经由古法语 durable 来自拉丁语 durabilis，后者由 durare「持续、忍耐」加 -abilis 构成；durare 又源于 durus「坚硬的、结实的」。同一词根还给出 duration、endure、durability。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of durable apply one idea of lasting to an object, to an agreement, and to a category of goods.
sensesIntro.cn: durable 的三个义项把同一个「持久」观念分别用到物品、协议和一类商品上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn boot whose sole still holds together after years of gravel.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双磨旧的靴子，鞋底在多年碎石之后仍然完好。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a material or product that resists wear and pressure.
branches.cn: 物品线：抵抗磨损与压力的材料或产品。

branches.en: THE BOND: an agreement or relationship that time does not wear through.
branches.cn: 纽带线：时间磨不穿的协议或关系。

branches.en: THE MARKET: a class of goods expected to serve for years.
branches.cn: 市场线：预期能使用多年的一类商品。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF WEAR: leather resists friction, while a promise resists time.
branches.cn: 两种磨损：皮革抵抗摩擦，承诺抵抗时间。

branches.en: THE LONG USE: durability is what turns an object into a long-term purchase.
branches.cn: 长期使用线：耐久性使一件物品成为长期投资。

intro.en: Durable is a Latin-derived adjective built from a verb root plus -able; English adds -ity and -ly.
intro.cn: durable 是源自拉丁语的形容词，由动词词根加 -able 构成；英语再加 -ity 与 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin durus, durare and durabilis are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 durus、durare、durabilis 均有记录，只有更早的印欧语词根属于重构。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of resistance.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「抵抗」的观念。

items.example: It is the adjective behind the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族背后的形容词。
它提供时间层面的含义。

items.meaning: able to be or to do
items.example: It forms durabilis and English durable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成拉丁语 durabilis 与英语 durable。

items.example: It forms duration from the same root.

items.exampleCN: 它与 durus 共享词根。

latinEntries.meaning: to last, to endure, to remain hard

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「耐久性；耐用性」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「耐久地；持久地」
与 durable 同出拉丁语 durare，义为「持续时间；时长」

definition_zh: 持续时间；期间；音长
definition_en: the length of time that something continues, the period during which it happens, or the length of a sound
core_image: 一只沙漏，沙粒从上格漏到下格，量出一段有多长
scene: 手术室外的走廊里，家属盯着墙上的钟，秒针一圈圈过去。The duration of the operation was about four hours.
sceneCN: 这里 duration 是「持续时间」（第 1 个义项：某事从开始到结束所经过的时间）；句意是手术持续了大约四个小时。

pos.zh: 名词：持续时间；期间；音长

derivatives.zh: 与 duration 同出拉丁语 durare，义为「耐用的；持久的」
由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「持续时间的；时长的」
由本词同源词加 -ive 构成，义为「持续性的（语法术语）」

senses.title: Length of time
senses.definition: the length of time that something continues or is expected to continue
senses.definitionCN: 某事物持续或预期持续的时间长度
senses.example: The duration of the operation was about four hours.
senses.exampleCN: 手术持续了大约四个小时。
senses.why: Latin durare meant to last, and -ation turns that lasting into a measurable quantity, like sand in a glass.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 durare 意为「持续」，-ation 把这种持续变成一个可测量的量，像玻璃里的沙。

senses.title: A particular period
senses.definition: the period during which something happens, especially a war, a course or a contract
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生的整段时间，尤指战争、课程或合同
senses.example: She stayed for the duration of the conference.
senses.exampleCN: 会议期间她一直留在那里。
senses.why: The measured length also names the stretch of time itself, so duration can mean the whole period covered.
senses.whyCN: 被测量出的长度也可以指那段时间本身，所以 duration 也能表示整个覆盖的时期。

senses.title: Length of a sound
senses.definition: the amount of time a speech sound or musical note is held, used in phonetics and music
senses.definitionCN: 语音或音符被持续的时间，用于语音学与音乐
senses.example: In this language, vowel duration can change the meaning of a word.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种语言里，元音的音长能改变词义。
senses.why: Phonetics borrowed the general word because a held sound is simply a duration that can be measured on a machine.
senses.whyCN: 语音学借用了这个通用词，因为一个被拉长的声音就是一段可以在仪器上量出的时长。

intro.en: Duration comes from Latin duratio, a lasting, which was built on durare, to last, and entered English through French.
intro.cn: duration 来自拉丁语 duratio（持续），由 durare（持续）构成，经由法语进入英语。

items.en: Latin durus meant hard or firm, and from it came the idea of holding out or lasting.
items.cn: 拉丁语 durus 意为「坚硬、结实」，由此产生「撑住、持续」的观念。

items.en: The verb durare meant to last or to endure, and it is the direct root of the whole family.
items.cn: 动词 durare 意为「持续、忍耐」，是整个词族的直接词根。

items.en: The noun duratio named the act or state of lasting, and it is the direct source of duration.
items.cn: 名词 duratio 指「持续」的动作或状态，是 duration 的直接来源。

items.en: A French form of the Latin noun carried it toward English, where the spelling settled as duration.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词的法语形式把它带向英语，拼写最终固定为 duration。

items.en: The word is recorded in English by the late fourteenth century, first in learned and legal writing.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪晚期见于英语，最初用于学术和法律文本。

items.en: Everyday use added for the duration, while phonetics and music kept the technical sense of held length.
items.cn: 日常用法增加了 for the duration 这一短语，语音学与音乐则保留了「拉长的时间」这一技术义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin lasting root; the near-meaning group separates length, period, term and span by what they measure.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「持续」词族的词；近义组按所测量的对象区分 length、period、term 与 span。

entries.definition: Able to last a long time; it describes the object, while duration measures the time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「耐用的、持久的」，描述物体本身，而 duration 测量的是时间。

entries.definition: Throughout or within a period; it began as 'while lasting' from the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……期间」，最初由同一动词的「当其持续时」演变而来。

entries.definition: Relating to duration or length of time; duration plus -al.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「持续时间的、时长的」，由 duration 加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: To last through difficulty or to bear it; related through Latin durus.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「忍受、持续」，经由拉丁语 durus 同源。

entries.definition: The measured extent of time or space; more general than duration.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「长度、时长」，比 duration 更通用。

entries.definition: A stretch of time with a beginning and an end; it can also name an era.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「时期、阶段」，有始有终，也可指一个时代。

entries.definition: A fixed length of time, as of a contract, school year or office; it stresses the limit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「期限、任期」，强调固定的时限。

entries.definition: The full extent from beginning to end, as of a life or a bridge; it stresses the whole reach.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「跨度、全程」，强调从始到终的整体范围。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie duration to the Latin verb for lasting and to the image of sand running through a glass.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 duration 连到表示「持续」的拉丁动词，以及沙粒流过沙漏的画面。

normal.en: durare is to last; duration is the amount of lasting measured out.
normal.cn: durare 是「持续」，duration 就是量出来的持续长度。

normal.en: The suffix -ation turns the verb into a noun of process and result.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ation 把动词变成表示过程与结果的名词。

normal.en: The same root gives durable, during and endure, so the family all points at time.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 durable、during 与 endure，这一族都指向时间。

normal.en: For the duration means for the whole time, until the end.
normal.cn: for the duration 意为在整个期间，直到结束。

normal.en: A long vowel has a longer duration than a short one, which is why phonetics uses the word.
normal.cn: 长元音的 duration 比短元音长，所以语音学用这个词。

abstract.en: Picture an hourglass: the amount of sand that has fallen is the duration already spent.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沙漏：已落下的沙量就是已经耗掉的 duration。

abstract.en: Turn the glass over and the same sand becomes a period with a beginning and an end.
abstract.cn: 把沙漏翻转，同一堆沙就变成有始有终的一段时间。

abstract.en: Duration is time made countable, one grain after another.
abstract.cn: duration 是被变得可数的时间，一粒沙接着一粒沙。

examples.en: The duration of the flight is about eleven hours.
examples.cn: 这次飞行的时长约为十一小时。

examples.en: She stayed for the duration of the conference.
examples.cn: 会议期间她一直留在那里。

examples.en: The drug reduces the duration of the illness.
examples.cn: 这种药能缩短病程。

dict_mnemonic.text: dur- 是「持续」，-ation 是名词后缀：duration 就是「持续出来的那段时间」。

root: 来自拉丁语 duratio「持续」，由动词 durare「持续、忍耐」加名词后缀构成，durare 又源于 durus「坚硬的」。经由法语进入英语，十四世纪晚期已有记录；同族词包括 durable、during、endure。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of duration all measure or name a stretch of time: a length, a whole period, or the held length of a sound.
sensesIntro.cn: duration 的三个义项都在测量或命名一段时间：一个长度、一整段时期，或一个声音被拉长的时长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sand running through an hourglass, measuring how long a thing lasts.
core.cn: 核心意象：沙粒流过沙漏，量出某物持续多久。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: the amount of time from start to finish.
branches.cn: 度量线：从开始到结束的时间总量。

branches.en: THE PERIOD: the whole stretch during which an event or contract runs.
branches.cn: 时期线：某一事件或合同持续覆盖的整段时间。

branches.en: THE SOUND: a held vowel or note measured on a machine.
branches.cn: 声音线：在仪器上量出的拉长元音或音符。

branches.en: LENGTH AND PERIOD: one is the number, the other is the stretch it describes.
branches.cn: 长度与时期：一个是数字，另一个是数字所描述的那一段。

branches.en: SMALL AND LARGE SCALES: a war lasts years, a vowel lasts milliseconds, and both are durations.
branches.cn: 大小尺度：战争持续数年，元音持续毫秒，两者都是 duration。

intro.en: Duration is a Latin-derived noun: a verb root plus -ation, with relatives built on -able and -al.
intro.cn: duration 是源自拉丁语的名词：动词词根加 -ation，亲属词则由 -able 与 -al 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin durus, durare, duratio and durabilis are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 durus、durare、duratio、durabilis 均有记录，只有更早的印欧语词根属于重构。

items.example: The root supplies the sense of holding out.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「撑住」的含义。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的直接来源。
它把 durare 变成 duratio。

items.example: It appears in the English ending -tion.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在英语的 -tion 词尾中。

items.example: It forms during from the old verb dure.
items.exampleCN: 它由旧动词 dure 构成 during。

derivatives.zh: 与 duration 同出拉丁语 durare，义为「耐用的；持久的」
由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「持续时间的；时长的」
由本词同源词加 -ive 构成，义为「持续性的（语法术语）」

definition_zh: 在……期间；在……过程中
definition_en: throughout a period, at some point within a period, or in the course of an event or activity
core_image: 一条时间线被括号括住，事情就发生在这段括号里
scene: 窗外雷声滚过，屋里的灯忽然灭了，黑暗中有人摸索着找蜡烛。The lights went out during the storm.
sceneCN: 这里 during 是「在……期间」（第 1 个义项：贯穿某段时间）；句意是暴风雨期间灯灭了。

pos.zh: 介词：在……期间；在……过程中

derivatives.zh: 与 during 同出拉丁语 durare，义为「耐用的；持久的」
与 during 同源，义为「持续时间；期间」

senses.title: Throughout a period
senses.definition: for the whole of a period of time, from its beginning to its end
senses.definitionCN: 在某段时间的整段之内，从开始到结束
senses.example: The lights went out during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨期间灯灭了。
senses.why: During began as the present participle of a verb meaning to last, so it literally places an event 'while the period is lasting'.
senses.whyCN: during 最初是表示「持续」的动词的现在分词，字面上就是把事件放在「那段时间正持续着」的时候。

senses.title: At a point within a period
senses.definition: at some unspecified moment inside a period, not necessarily for all of it
senses.definitionCN: 在某段时间内某个未指明的时刻，不一定是整段
senses.example: He fell asleep during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座期间他睡着了。
senses.why: A point event can sit anywhere inside the bracket of the period, and during covers that inside without fixing the exact moment.
senses.whyCN: 一个瞬时事件可以落在这一时期的括号内任意位置，during 覆盖这个「里面」，却不指明确切时刻。

senses.title: In the course of an activity
senses.definition: while an activity, process or event is going on, especially one with a clear course
senses.definitionCN: 在某项活动、过程或事件进行之时，尤指有明确进程的事
senses.example: During the course, students work in small groups.
senses.exampleCN: 课程过程中，学生们分成小组活动。
senses.why: The period can also be an activity with stages, and during then marks the span in which those stages unfold.
senses.whyCN: 这一时期也可以是一项有阶段的活动，during 就标出这些阶段展开的那段时间。

intro.en: During is the present participle of an obsolete English verb dure, to last, which came from Latin durare through French.
intro.cn: during 是英语旧动词 dure（持续）的现在分词，后者经由法语来自拉丁语 durare。

items.en: Latin durare meant to last or to endure and is the root of duration and durable as well.
items.cn: 拉丁语 durare 意为「持续、忍耐」，也是 duration 与 durable 的词根。

items.en: Old French durer meant to last, and English borrowed it as the verb dure.
items.cn: 古法语 durer 意为「持续」，英语把它借来作动词 dure。

items.en: The English verb dure, to last, is now obsolete but was common in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries.
items.cn: 英语动词 dure（持续）如今已废弃，但在十四、十五世纪很常见。

items.en: The form during meant 'while lasting', and from that phrase it became a preposition of time.
items.cn: 形式 during 原意是「当其持续时」，由此变成一个表示时间的介词。

items.en: During is recorded as a preposition by the late fourteenth century, usually with a period or an activity.
items.cn: during 在十四世纪晚期已记录为介词，通常后接一段时期或一项活动。

items.en: The old verb disappeared, but the participle survived as one of the most common time words in English.
items.cn: 旧动词消失了，但这个分词存活下来，成为英语中最常用的时间词之一。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same lasting root; the near-meaning group separates throughout, while and amid by scope and register.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「持续」词族的词；近义组按范围与语体区分 throughout、while 与 amid。

entries.definition: The length of time something lasts; the noun behind the preposition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「持续时间」，是这个介词背后的名词。

entries.definition: Able to last a long time; it describes objects rather than time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「耐用的、持久的」，描述物体而非时间。

entries.definition: To last through hardship or to bear it; a verb from the same Latin family.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「忍受、持续」，属同一拉丁词族。

entries.definition: An obsolete English verb meaning to last; the form from which during was made.
entries.definitionCN: 旧时英语动词，义为「持续」，正是构成 during 的那个形式。

entries.definition: In every part of a period or place; stronger than during because it excludes gaps.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「贯穿整个期间或各处」，比 during 更强，排除间断。

entries.definition: During the time that something else is happening; it usually joins two clauses.
entries.definitionCN: 连词，义为「当……时」，通常连接两个分句。

entries.definition: In the middle of an event or situation; more formal and often literary.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……之中」，更正式，常带文学色彩。

entries.definition: Inside a period or limit; it stresses the boundary rather than the whole span.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……之内」，强调边界而非整段。

normalIntro.en: These hooks remember that during was once a participle meaning 'while lasting', then show how it brackets a period.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子记住 during 原是意为「当其持续时」的分词，再展示它如何把一段时间括起来。

normal.en: During was born from dure, to last: it marks the time while something lasts.
normal.cn: during 出自 dure（持续），标记某事物持续着的那段时间。

normal.en: Think of a pair of brackets around a timeline: everything inside happens during it.
normal.cn: 想象在一条时间线上画一对括号：括号里发生的事就是 during 它。

normal.en: During the war covers the whole period; during the lecture can be one moment inside it.
normal.cn: during the war 覆盖整段时期，during the lecture 可以是其中某一刻。

normal.en: Do not confuse during with for: during names the period, for names the length.
normal.cn: 不要把 during 与 for 混淆：during 指那段时间，for 指长度。

normal.en: The same family gives duration and durable, so time is the shared idea.
normal.cn: 同一词族给出 duration 与 durable，共同观念就是时间。

abstract.en: Picture two hands holding a stretch of a timeline, with an event placed between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手捏住时间线上的一段，把一件事放在两手之间。

abstract.en: The bracket can be wide as a war or narrow as a single breath.
abstract.cn: 这个括号可以宽如一场战争，也可以窄如一息。

abstract.en: During never says how long; it only says inside which period.
abstract.cn: during 从不说多久，只说在哪段时期之内。

examples.en: The lights went out during the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨期间灯灭了。

examples.en: He fell asleep during the lecture.
examples.cn: 讲座期间他睡着了。

examples.en: During the war, the family lived in the countryside.
examples.cn: 战争期间，这家人住在乡下。

dict_mnemonic.text: during 原是「持续」的现在分词：某事持续着的那段时间，就是 during 它。

root: 英语旧动词 dure「持续」的现在分词，dure 经由古法语 durer 来自拉丁语 durare「持续、忍耐」。during 原意「当其持续时」，十四世纪晚期起用作时间介词；同族词有 duration、durable、endure。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of during all place an event inside a period: across the whole of it, at a point within it, or in the course of an activity.
sensesIntro.cn: during 的三个义项都把事件放进一段时间里：贯穿整段、落在其中某一刻，或在一项活动的过程中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stretch of timeline held between two brackets.
core.cn: 核心意象：时间线上被一对括号括住的一段。

branches.en: THE WHOLE BRACKET: an event fills the entire period from start to end.
branches.cn: 整段括号线：事件从开始到结束填满整个时期。

branches.en: THE POINT INSIDE: a brief event happens somewhere within the bracket.
branches.cn: 括号内一点线：短暂事件发生在括号内的某处。

branches.en: THE COURSE: the period is an activity with stages unfolding.
branches.cn: 过程线：这段时期是一项分阶段展开的活动。

branches.en: TWO WIDTHS: a war or a course can both be bracketed, at different scales.
branches.cn: 两种宽度：战争与课程都能被括住，只是尺度不同。

branches.en: ONE MOMENT IN A PROCESS: the point event sits inside a longer course.
branches.cn: 过程里的一刻：瞬时事件落在一段更长的过程之中。

intro.en: During is a fossilised participle: the suffix -ing survives on an old verb that English otherwise dropped.
intro.cn: during 是一个凝固的分词：-ing 后缀留在一个英语其他场合已丢弃的旧动词上。

latinIntro.en: Latin durare and duratio are recorded; the English verb dure came through Old French and then disappeared.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 durare 与 duratio 均有记录；英语动词 dure 经由古法语而来，后来消失。

items.example: The root is shared with duration and durable.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根与 duration、durable 共用。

items.example: It is the ultimate source of during.
items.exampleCN: 它是 during 的最终来源。

items.example: The verb supplied the participle during.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了分词 during。
它由 dure 构成 during。

items.example: It shares the same Latin root.
items.exampleCN: 它与 during 共享同一拉丁词根。

derivatives.zh: 与 during 同出拉丁语 durare，义为「耐用的；持久的」
与 during 同源，义为「持续时间；期间」

definition_zh: 黄昏；薄暮；暮色；昏暗
definition_en: the time when day is ending and night is beginning, the dim light of that time, or a dark shadowy state
core_image: 山脊上的颜色一点点褪去，天边只剩一层薄薄的灰蓝
scene: 山脊上的颜色一点点褪去，鸟群开始向林中飞去。The birds returned to the trees at dusk.
sceneCN: 这里 dusk 是「黄昏」（第 1 个义项：白昼将尽、夜晚初临的时刻）；句意是黄昏时鸟群飞回了林中。

pos.zh: 名词：黄昏；薄暮；暮色

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「昏暗的；暮色的」
由 dusky 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「昏暗；暮色」
由本词加 -ish 构成，义为「略带暮色的；微暗的」

senses.title: The time when day ends
senses.definition: the time of day when the sun has set or is setting and night is beginning
senses.definitionCN: 太阳已落或正在落下、夜晚开始的时刻
senses.example: The birds returned to the trees at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时鸟群飞回了林中。
senses.why: Dusk began as an adjective for darkness; the noun then named the hour when that darkness first settles.
senses.whyCN: dusk 最初是表示「昏暗」的形容词，名词随后命名那片昏暗初次落下的时刻。

senses.title: The dim light of that hour
senses.definition: the soft, dim light seen in the sky just after sunset or just before night
senses.definitionCN: 日落后或入夜前天空中那种柔和而暗淡的光
senses.example: The dusk light made the road hard to see.
senses.exampleCN: 暮色让路很难看清。
senses.why: The hour and the light it contains are named together, so dusk can mean the glow as well as the time.
senses.whyCN: 那个时辰与它包含的光被一起命名，所以 dusk 既可指时刻，也可指那层光。

senses.title: A dark, shadowy state
senses.definition: a state of darkness or gloom, used mainly in literary writing
senses.definitionCN: 昏暗或阴郁的状态，主要用于书面文学
senses.example: The room lay in the dusk of drawn curtains.
senses.exampleCN: 房间笼罩在拉上窗帘后的幽暗里。
senses.why: Literature extends the evening image indoors: any half-dark place can be described as being in dusk.
senses.whyCN: 文学把黄昏的意象移到室内：任何半暗的地方都可以说处在 dusk 里。

intro.en: Dusk is an Old English word for dark or swarthy; the modern noun for twilight developed later from that adjective.
intro.cn: dusk 是古英语中表示「昏暗、黝黑」的词；现代表示「暮色」的名词义是后来从这个形容词发展出来的。

items.en: Old English dox or dusce described something dark, swarthy or shadowy, especially colour.
items.cn: 古英语 dox 或 dusce 形容昏暗、黝黑或阴影般的，尤其指颜色。

items.en: Middle English kept the adjective sense of dark and dim, applied to light and to surfaces.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了「昏暗、暗淡」的形容词义，用于光和表面。

items.en: The noun dusk for the twilight hour is recorded in the seventeenth century, growing from the adjective.
items.cn: 表示黄昏时刻的名词 dusk 在十七世纪有记录，是从形容词发展来的。

items.en: Literary writing extended dusk to any shadowy half-light, including indoor gloom.
items.cn: 文学写作把 dusk 扩展到任何幽暗的半光，包括室内的阴郁。

items.en: At dusk, dusk falls and from dusk till dawn fixed the word in everyday time expressions.
items.cn: at dusk、dusk falls 与 from dusk till dawn 把这个词固定在日常时间表达里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on dusk and one near-spelling word; the near-meaning group separates twilight, sunset and nightfall by exact time.
note.cn: 形近组收由 dusk 构成的词形和一个拼写相近的词；近义组按确切时段区分 twilight、sunset 与 nightfall。

entries.definition: Dark or dim, often with a soft or slightly sad tone; dusk plus -y.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「昏暗的、暮色的」，常带柔和或微带忧伤的语气，由 dusk 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: The quality of being dark or dim; dusky plus -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「昏暗、幽暗」，由 dusky 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: Slightly dark or dim; dusk plus the softening suffix -ish.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「微暗的、略带暮色的」，由 dusk 加弱化后缀 -ish 构成。

entries.definition: Fine dry particles of earth; it looks close to dusk but is a different noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「灰尘」，拼写与 dusk 接近，却是另一个名词。

entries.definition: The soft light between sunset and darkness, or between darkness and sunrise; wider than dusk.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「暮光、曙光」，指日落到黑暗之间或黑暗到日出之间的柔光，范围比 dusk 更宽。

entries.definition: The moment the sun disappears below the horizon; it marks the start of dusk.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「日落」，指太阳沉到地平线以下的时刻，是黄昏的开端。

entries.definition: The moment night begins; later and darker than dusk.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「入夜」，指夜晚开始的时刻，比黄昏更晚、更暗。

entries.definition: The later part of the day, from late afternoon to night; much broader than dusk.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「傍晚、晚上」，指一天的后半段，范围比 dusk 宽得多。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from the old adjective for dark and then narrow it to the hour when darkness first falls.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从表示「昏暗」的古老形容词出发，再收窄到黑暗最初落下的那个时辰。

normal.en: Dusk first meant dark as an adjective, then became the name of the darkening hour.
normal.cn: dusk 最初作形容词表示「昏暗」，后来变成那个渐渐变暗的时辰的名字。

normal.en: At dusk is the fixed phrase; dusk falls is the picture of the light giving way.
normal.cn: at dusk 是固定说法，dusk falls 是光线让位的画面。

normal.en: Dusk sits between sunset and nightfall: not yet night, no longer day.
normal.cn: dusk 位于日落与入夜之间：还不是夜，也不再是白天。

normal.en: Dusky is the adjective, duskiness the noun: the family keeps the dim light.
normal.cn: dusky 是形容词，duskiness 是名词，这一族都保留着那层昏暗的光。

normal.en: From dusk till dawn covers the whole night between two soft lights.
normal.cn: from dusk till dawn 覆盖两片柔光之间的整个夜晚。

abstract.en: Picture a hillside where colour drains away and only a grey-blue band remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一面山坡，颜色一点点褪去，只剩一条灰蓝的带子。

abstract.en: The same band appears indoors behind drawn curtains, as a room fills with half-light.
abstract.cn: 同一条带子又出现在拉上窗帘的室内，房间被半光填满。

abstract.en: Dusk is the seam between day and night, where neither one fully holds.
abstract.cn: dusk 是白昼与夜晚之间的接缝，两边都还未完全占住。

examples.en: The birds returned to the trees at dusk.
examples.cn: 黄昏时鸟群飞回了林中。

examples.en: By dusk the market had emptied.
examples.cn: 到黄昏时，市场已经空了。

examples.en: The dusk light made the road hard to see.
examples.cn: 暮色让路很难看清。

dict_mnemonic.text: dusk 是太阳落下后那层灰蓝的薄光：白天用尽，夜晚还没完全接手。

root: 古英语 dox 或 dusce 形容「昏暗、黝黑」，中古英语保留形容词义；十七世纪起名词 dusk 指黄昏时刻，十八至十九世纪文学又把它扩展到任何幽暗的半光。与 dust 拼写相近但来源不同。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of dusk move from the hour, to the light inside it, to any shadowy half-dark.
sensesIntro.cn: dusk 的三个义项从那个时辰，移到时辰里的光，再移到任何幽暗的半黑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hillside losing its colour as a thin grey-blue band remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：山坡褪去颜色，只剩一条薄薄的灰蓝。

branches.en: THE HOUR: the moment when day ends and night begins.
branches.cn: 时辰线：白昼结束、夜晚开始的时刻。

branches.en: THE LIGHT: the soft dim glow left in the sky at that hour.
branches.cn: 光线线：那个时辰天空里留下的柔和暗光。

branches.en: THE GLOOM: any shadowy half-dark, especially indoors in literature.
branches.cn: 幽暗线：任何阴影般的半黑，尤指文学中的室内。

branches.en: TIME AND GLOW: the word names both the hour and what fills it.
branches.cn: 时辰与光：这个词同时命名那个时刻和充满它的光。

branches.en: FROM SKY TO ROOM: the same dim light is carried indoors as gloom.
branches.cn: 从天空到室内：同一种暗光被带进屋里，成为幽暗。

intro.en: Dusk is a native English word; English adds -y, -ness and -ish, and fixed phrases carry most of its use.
intro.cn: dusk 是本族语英语词；英语加 -y、-ness、-ish，而它的用法多由固定短语承担。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; Latin crepusculum, twilight, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 crepusculum（暮色）只是语义上的对应。

items.example: The word began as an adjective and became a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从形容词开始，后来成为名词。
它出现在 dusk falls 中。

items.example: It appears in from dusk till dawn.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 from dusk till dawn 中。
它出现在 at dusk 中。
它出现在 by dusk 中。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「昏暗的；暮色的」
由 dusky 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「昏暗；暮色」
由本词加 -ish 构成，义为「略带暮色的；微暗的」

definition_zh: 灰尘；尘土；掸去灰尘；撒（粉末）；（书面）尘土、遗骸
definition_en: fine dry particles of earth or other material, household dirt, the act of removing it, or to scatter a powder over something
core_image: 阳光斜穿过窗缝，空气里浮着无数细小的颗粒
scene: 阳光从窗缝里照进来，空气里浮着细小的颗粒，落在架子上。Dust covered every shelf in the old room.
sceneCN: 这里 dust 是「灰尘」（第 1 个义项：细干的土状颗粒）；句意是灰尘盖满了那间旧屋的每一层书架。

pos.zh: 名词：灰尘；尘土；粉末
动词：掸去灰尘；撒（粉末）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「布满灰尘的；土色的」
由本词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「抹布；掸子」
由本词与 pan 复合，义为「簸箕」

senses.title: Fine dry particles
senses.definition: fine dry particles of earth, rock or other material that can float in the air or settle on surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 细干土、岩石或其他材料构成的颗粒，能浮在空气中或落在表面
senses.example: Dust covered every shelf in the old room.
senses.exampleCN: 灰尘盖满了那间旧屋的每一层书架。
senses.why: This is the physical core: matter reduced to particles small enough to be carried by air and to settle everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理核心：物质被碎成小到能被空气携带、又能落得到处都是的颗粒。

senses.title: A cloud of particles
senses.definition: a mass of dust lifted into the air, as by wind, traffic or an explosion
senses.definitionCN: 被风、车流或爆炸扬到空中的一团尘土
senses.example: A cloud of dust rose from the dry road.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥的路面上扬起一团尘土。
senses.why: The same particles, once airborne, become a visible body; the noun then names the cloud rather than the surface layer.
senses.whyCN: 同样的颗粒一旦升空就成了一团可见的物体，名词于是指这团云，而不是表面那层。

senses.title: To remove dust
senses.definition: to wipe or brush dust from a surface, or to clean a room of it
senses.definitionCN: 把灰尘从表面擦掉或掸掉，或清扫房间里的灰
senses.example: She dusted the furniture before the guests arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 客人到之前，她掸去了家具上的灰。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: the particles are there, and the action takes them away.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词反过来：颗粒已经在那里，动作则把它们拿走。

senses.title: To scatter a powder
senses.definition: to scatter a fine powder over something, as sugar, flour or a chemical
senses.definitionCN: 把细粉撒在某物上，如糖、面粉或化学品
senses.example: Dust the cake with a little sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 在蛋糕上撒一点糖。
senses.why: If dust can be removed, it can also be applied: the verb works in both directions, taking away or sprinkling on.
senses.whyCN: 既然灰尘能被去掉，也能被施加：这个动词两个方向都成立，拿走或者撒上。

senses.title: The ground or mortal remains
senses.definition: used in literary and religious language for the ground, the human body or what remains of it
senses.definitionCN: 用于文学与宗教语言，指土地、人体或其遗留之物
senses.example: The old prayer repeats that we are dust and return to dust.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇古老的祷文反复说，我们本是尘土，也要归于尘土。
senses.why: Because the body returns to the ground, dust became a solemn image for mortality, fixed in the phrase dust to dust.
senses.whyCN: 因为身体归入土地，dust 成了关于必死的庄重意象，固定在 dust to dust 这一短语里。

intro.en: Dust is an Old English noun shared across the Germanic languages; the verb came later from the noun.
intro.cn: dust 是古英语名词，为多种日耳曼语言共有；动词是后来从名词变来的。

items.en: The word is sometimes connected with a root for smoke or fine vapour, but the evidence is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词有时被联系到一个表示「烟、细雾」的词根，但证据不确定。

items.en: The Germanic noun for dust is reconstructed in a form close to dustam, with relatives in several modern languages.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中表示「灰尘」的名词被重构为接近 dustam 的形式，在多种现代语言中都有亲属词。

items.en: Old English dust meant dust or powder, and it was already used in religious language about the body.
items.cn: 古英语 dust 意为「灰尘、粉末」，当时已用于关于身体的宗教语言。

items.en: Middle English kept the noun and added the verb sense of sprinkling powder or removing dust.
items.cn: 中古英语保留名词，并增加「撒粉」与「掸灰」两个动词义。

items.en: The verb dust is recorded as both removing dust and applying powder, two opposite actions.
items.cn: 动词 dust 在十六世纪已有记录，既指去掉灰尘，也指撒上粉末，两个方向相反。

items.en: Dust storm, gold dust and dust to dust show the word spread across weather, trade and ritual.
items.cn: dust storm、gold dust 与 dust to dust 展示了这个词横跨天气、贸易与仪式。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on dust; the near-meaning group separates dirt, powder and soot by what they are made of.
note.cn: 形近组收由 dust 构成的词形；近义组按构成区分 dirt、powder 与 soot。

entries.definition: Covered with or full of dust; dust plus -y.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「布满灰尘的」，由 dust 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: A cloth or brush for removing dust; dust plus -er.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「抹布、掸子」，由 dust 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A flat container used with a brush to collect dust and dirt.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「簸箕」，与扫帚配合收集灰尘和脏物。

entries.definition: A container for household rubbish; dust plus bin, common in British English.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垃圾桶」，由 dust 加 bin 构成，常见于英式英语。

entries.definition: Unclean matter such as mud or grime; it is coarser and often wetter than dust.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「污物、泥垢」，比 dust 更粗、更常带湿。

entries.definition: A dry substance ground into fine particles; it may be clean and deliberate, unlike dust.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「粉末」，指磨成细颗粒的干燥物质，可能是干净且有意制成的。

entries.definition: Black powder left by smoke; a specific kind of dust from burning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「烟灰、煤烟」，是燃烧留下的一种特定灰尘。

entries.definition: Small hard particles of stone or sand; coarser and heavier than dust.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「砂砾」，指石或沙的小硬颗粒，比 dust 更粗更重。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the particles from the air to the shelf, then show the verb working in two opposite directions.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着颗粒从空气落到架子上，再展示动词两个相反的用法。

normal.en: Dust is matter small enough to float and settle: start with a sunbeam full of specks.
normal.cn: dust 是小到能漂浮、能落下的物质：先从一道满是细点的阳光开始。

normal.en: The verb dust can mean remove dust or add powder, so the object tells you the direction.
normal.cn: 动词 dust 既可指去掉灰尘，也可指撒上粉末，看宾语就知道方向。

normal.en: Dusty, duster and dustpan all keep the same particles in view.
normal.cn: dusty、duster 与 dustpan 都围着同样的颗粒。

normal.en: A dust storm is a whole sky turned into a cloud of particles.
normal.cn: dust storm 是一整片天空都变成颗粒的云。

normal.en: Dust to dust is the solemn phrase for the body returning to the ground.
normal.cn: dust to dust 是身体回归土地的庄重短语。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow beam of light crossing a room, every speck suddenly visible.
abstract.cn: 想象一道穿过房间的窄光，每一粒微尘忽然都看得见。

abstract.en: The same specks settle on a shelf, then rise again as a cloud over a dry road.
abstract.cn: 同样的微粒落在架子上，又在干燥的路面上重新升成一团云。

abstract.en: Dust is matter at its smallest and most patient, waiting on every surface.
abstract.cn: dust 是物质最小、最有耐心的形态，等在每一个表面上。

examples.en: Dust covered every shelf in the old room.
examples.cn: 灰尘盖满了那间旧屋的每一层书架。

examples.en: She dusted the furniture before the guests arrived.
examples.cn: 客人到之前，她掸去了家具上的灰。

examples.en: A cloud of dust rose from the dry road.
examples.cn: 干燥的路面上扬起一团尘土。

dict_mnemonic.text: dust 是阳光里浮动的细颗粒：落在架上是灰，扬在空中是尘，擦掉是掸灰，撒上是撒粉。

root: 古英语 dust「灰尘、粉末」，为日耳曼语共有词，重构形式接近 dustam；中古英语增加「撒粉」与「掸灰」的动词义，十六世纪两种相反用法均有记录。更早的印欧语来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of dust all centre on fine particles: settled on a surface, lifted as a cloud, wiped away, sprinkled on, or returned to the ground.
sensesIntro.cn: dust 的五个义项都围绕细小颗粒：落在表面、扬成云、被擦掉、被撒上，或回归土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: specks of matter floating in a beam of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束光里浮动的微小颗粒。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: particles that settle on shelves, roads and windows.
branches.cn: 表面线：落在书架、道路和窗上的颗粒。

branches.en: THE AIR: the same particles lifted into a visible cloud.
branches.cn: 空气线：同样的颗粒被扬成一团看得见的云。

branches.en: THE HAND: the verb can take dust away or put powder on.
branches.cn: 手线：动词既能拿走灰尘，也能撒上粉末。

branches.en: TWO STATES: settled dust and flying dust are the same matter in different motion.
branches.cn: 两种状态：落定的灰与飞扬的尘是同一物质的不同运动。

branches.en: THE RITUAL: dust becomes a solemn image for the body and the ground.
branches.cn: 仪式线：dust 成为身体与土地的庄重意象。

intro.en: Dust is a native Germanic noun; English adds -y, -er, -ed, -ing and compounds such as dustpan and dustbin.
intro.cn: dust 是本族语日耳曼语名词；英语加 -y、-er、-ed、-ing，并构成 dustpan、dustbin 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; Latin pulvis, dust, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 pulvis（灰尘）只是语义上的对应。

items.example: The noun is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的基础。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「布满灰尘的；土色的」
由本词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「抹布；掸子」
由本词与 pan 复合，义为「簸箕」
